To make sure there are no leaks, on the client, block traffic on all interfaces except the VPN's one via iptables (or whatever firewall you use). For instance, my VPN traffic is on tun0, my VPS IP is x.x.x.x, and my (non-vpn) ethernet interface is enp3s0, so I have:

# Flush all rules
iptables -F
iptables -X

# Allow unlimited traffic on localhost (breaks MPI programs otherwise)
iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -o lo -j ACCEPT

# Allow incomming traffic from estabilished and related connections on TUN
iptables -A INPUT -i tun0 -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

# Allow outgoing and forward traffic on TUN
iptables -A OUTPUT -o tun0 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -o tun0 -j ACCEPT

# Allow traffic in other interfaces to the VPN ip only
iptables -A INPUT -i enp3s0 -s x.x.x.x -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -o enp3s0 -d x.x.x.x -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -o enp3s0 -d x.x.x.x -j ACCEPT

# Policy: Drop everything else
iptables -P OUTPUT DROP
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP
